Where things stand
I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt — 333 tracked files, every one SHA-256 verified against its metadata (only export.sh differs, because the dump self-documents it in two places). Two things I found before writing any code:

Slice 33 is already in the tree, and it has not been run yet. The commit is 8c0772c "add claude changes", and docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md carries the full Slice 33 section. But all three terminal logs are from Slice 32 — 1074 tests, 16 E2E scenarios, no Slice 33 numbers anywhere. So the tree currently holds one unverified slice. Worth knowing before a second one lands on top of it.

The next slice's work turned up three findings, and one of them blocks the plan's own next step. The plan says Stage 1b continues by emptying .chip and .visually-hidden from the remaining pages and extending SharedSelectorPrefixes to cover them in the same commit. I went to do exactly that and found:

F-65 — §11.12 names four kinds of control that carry the 44px target; app.css declares two of them at 36px. --touch-target is 2.75rem, and §11.12 says so of "buttons, links that act as buttons, checkbox rows, and the session links in the header". .session-link and .link-button both declare min-height: 2.25rem. Between them that is the sign-out control in the header of every page in both layouts, and the destructive action on four administration surfaces ("Revoke role", "Revoke display", "Take it off the menu"). The comment above .session-link says "they carry the §11.12 target height" and "Vertical padding rather than a min-height" — the declaration is a min-height, there is no vertical padding, and the height is 8px under. Both sentences are false about the three lines beneath them. Scenario 16 cannot see it: the reach selector covers a record row's action, a page-head action and a filter's submit, and none of those is ever a .link-button.

F-66 — the four detail surfaces are F-59's fifth copy. ManageMenuItem, ManagePerson, ManageTable and TableDisplays each declare their own inline copy of one .manage-* vocabulary — 20 duplicated rules — and where they overlap app.css they contradict it. .visually-hidden is the deprecated clip: rect(0,0,0,0) on all four, which is precisely the thing Slice 30 said it centralised in order to remove; the inline copy is later at equal specificity, so those four pages never got the clip-path version. .chip-warn is pinned to 
#fdecea/
#a3261c against the palette's 
#fbeaea/
#7f1d1d — a visibly different red on four screens. And five rules have drifted between copies (.manage-heading, .manage-rule, .manage-inline-form, and its input and select). The material half: .manage-inline-form input/select set padding: 0.45rem 0.6rem and no min-height and no font floor — so the one control each of those pages exists for is ~34px tall and will zoom an iPhone's viewport on focus and not zoom back.

F-67 — the gate that enforces "declared once" cannot tell a declaration from a comment. NoComponentRedeclaresTheSharedHandheldVocabulary substring-matches each prefix against the whole <style> block. It strips Razor comments and not CSS comments — while its sibling fact in the same file does strip them. KitchenBoard, CounterBoard and CounterSitting each mention .chip and .muted in a CSS comment explaining that those names are app.css's. So adding .chip and .muted to the prefix list, which Stage 1b requires, reports findings on three correct pages. The test already applies a "declared, not merely mentioned" standard — it just applies it to app.css and not to the components.

What I'd deliver, and one decision for you
Slice 34, as one archive: the shared .manage-* vocabulary lifted into app.css (keeping the name is safe here, unlike .admin-header, because every holder empties in the same commit); the two touch-target literals corrected and that comment rewritten; TableDisplays and ManageSitting converted, which empties StillExpectedToCarryRetiredTableVocabulary and turns it into an emptiness assertion; the three other manage pages' duplicate blocks deleted; the contract test's CSS-comment and declaration-position fix plus the extended prefix list plus a new fact for F-65; and scenario 16 extended to the detail surfaces it can reach.

The decision: scenario 16 can reach /administration/people/{id}, /administration/tables/{id} and /administration/tables/{id}/displays from identifiers the scenario already mints, and /administration/menu/{id} if CreateMenuItemAsync returns one. That takes the barrier from six surfaces to nine or ten and needs .manage-inline-form button in the reach selector. /administration/sittings/{id} stays unmeasured — a sitting needs a guest, a token and a join, which is scenario 3's arrangement — stated the way hidden-records already is. Say go and I'll build it that way; say index-only and the barrier stays at six and the four converted surfaces go unmeasured, which I'd record as an honest gap rather than pretend otherwise.

I have not written any files yet, so nothing to delete on your side from this turn.

Where I got to
I stopped mid-flight, so nothing is packaged yet — there is no archive to apply and nothing for you to delete. Here is the state of the work and the one thing you need to know before the next turn.

A compile error I introduced and have not yet fixed. EndToEndScenarios.cs still refers to HandheldAdministrationPaths at line 2319, and I renamed the field to HandheldAdministrationIndexPaths. It also now needs using System.Globalization; for the string.Create calls in the new path builder. Both are in my notes for the next turn, but I'm flagging them because a half-applied slice is worse than none.

What is done and verified in my sandbox:

app.css — the two touch-target literals corrected to var(--touch-target) with the false comment rewritten; the shared .manage-* detail vocabulary added, replacing four inline copies, with its wide layout in the single existing breakpoint. Brace-balanced, still exactly two media queries and exactly one width query.
TableDisplays.razor — rewritten. Shared page head with the pairing button as its own action, shared record list with four labelled cells, three page-private rules left. The harness's two handles (button:has-text('Generate pairing code'), p.pairing-code) are both preserved.
ManageSitting.razor — converted. .admin-header → .page-head, the bill table → a labelled record list, .muted/.numeric/headings/rules/corrections onto shared names, inline block cut to page-private rules only.
ManageMenuItem.razor, ManagePerson.razor, ManageTable.razor — inline stylesheets emptied entirely; the history table converted to a labelled record list. section.account-panel h1 kept intact on ManagePerson, because ReadAccountFactsAsync reads through it.
HandheldLayoutContractTests.cs — seven facts now. Prefix list extended to .manage-, .chip, .muted, .visually-hidden; the redeclaration scan reads declared selectors instead of block text; the staged list deleted in favour of an emptiness assertion; a new fact for the touch-target rule.
HandheldReach.cs — .manage-inline-form button added to the reach selector.
The evidence, such as it is from here:

All seven facts ported to Python and run. Against the delivered tree: all seven pass. Files to delete: none. No git add needed — no new files, no new directories, so git ls-files already sees everything the gates read. I verified this by extracting the archive over a fresh copy of your current tree: the result is byte-for-byte identical to the tree I tested.

Read this before you run it: Slice 33 is in the tree and has never been exercised — your terminal logs are all Slice 32's, 1074 tests. This slice sits on top of it. If the first run is red, both slices are candidates, and Slice 33 is the honest place to start.

The three findings
F-67 blocked the work. Adding .chip and .muted to SharedSelectorPrefixes — which the plan required — reported findings on KitchenBoard, CounterBoard and CounterSitting, all three correct. Each names the shared vocabulary it leans on in a CSS comment. The fact matched a prefix against the text of a <style> block, stripping Razor comments and not CSS ones — while the custom-property fact thirty lines below it in the same file stripped both. So the rule's reach was the set of shared names nobody had written a sentence about.

F-66 is F-59's fifth copy. Four pages each declared their own .manage-* vocabulary: twenty duplicated rules, five drifted. .visually-hidden was still the deprecated clip: rect(…) on all four — exactly what Slice 30 said centralising the name would remove. Chip colours pinned off-palette. And .manage-inline-form input/select had no min-height and no font floor, so the one control each page exists for was ~34px and zoomed an iPhone's viewport without zooming back.

F-65 came out of writing F-66's assertion. .session-link and .link-button both at min-height: 2.25rem — 36px against the 44 §11.12 names those exact controls in by name. Between them: sign-out in the header of every page in both layouts, and the destructive action on four administration surfaces. The comment above one said it carried the §11.12 height and used "vertical padding rather than a min-height", above three lines with a min-height and no padding.

What to watch
Scenario 16 is the one. It walks ten surfaces now instead of six, four of which nothing has ever laid out at 375px. Fifteen controls expected, floor fourteen. A red result there would be information rather than a regression this slice introduced — the message names the surface, the two numbers, and the widest element outside a scroll container.

dotnet test should read 1077 — arithmetic from 1074 plus Slice 33's two facts plus this slice's one, and a prediction about two unrun slices at once rather than an observation.

Evidence, such as it is from here
All seven contract facts ported and run: seven pass on the delivered tree, five fail on your current tree — 54 re-declarations across five components, two controls under the target, four record-list pages where seven are expected, two retired-vocabulary holders. Ten planted regressions, ten results as designed, including the one that must not fire: a CSS comment naming .chip and .muted, which is F-67 demonstrated rather than asserted.

One thing worth your attention in BUILD_PROGRESS.md: my Razor tag scanner's first version reported twenty-seven findings on correct files, because For="@(() => Input.Name)" has a > inside quotes and the match ended early. I fixed the scanner. Had I trusted it, I would have "corrected" five files that were right — which is the same mistake F-41 is about, made by the tool built to prevent it.

Nothing compiled. No browser rendered anything. The four detail surfaces' compliance rests on reading app.css.
